front: In concurrent programming, what do safety, liveness, and performance each ask?
back: Safety asks whether anything bad can happen; liveness asks whether useful progress eventually happens; performance asks whether progress happens efficiently.
accepted_answers: Safety asks whether anything bad can happen; liveness asks whether useful progress eventually happens; performance asks whether progress happens efficiently.
hint: Think correctness, forward progress, and efficiency.

front: Why can code that works reliably in a single-threaded test still fail under concurrent load?
back: Multiple threads can interleave operations, observe stale state, or depend on timing in ways that never occur in a single-threaded run.
accepted_answers: Multiple threads can interleave operations, observe stale state, or depend on timing in ways that never occur in a single-threaded run.
hint: Look beyond simultaneous execution to visibility and ordering.

front: A server creates one platform thread for every incoming request with no bound. What production risk appears first under overload?
back: Resource exhaustion and collapse: too many threads consume memory and scheduling capacity, increasing context switching and making the server degrade unpredictably.
accepted_answers: Resource exhaustion and collapse: too many threads consume memory and scheduling capacity, increasing context switching and making the server degrade unpredictably.
hint: Concurrency can increase throughput until thread creation itself becomes the bottleneck.

front: What is a race condition?
back: A correctness failure where the result depends on the relative timing or interleaving of operations by multiple threads.
accepted_answers: ["A result that depends on thread timing or interleaving","A correctness failure depending on relative timing","race condition"]
hint: The same inputs may produce different results depending on scheduling.

front: What does it mean for a class to be thread-safe?
back: It behaves correctly when accessed by multiple threads, regardless of scheduling or interleaving, without requiring callers to add their own synchronization.
accepted_answers: It behaves correctly when accessed by multiple threads, regardless of scheduling or interleaving, without requiring callers to add their own synchronization.
hint: The guarantee belongs to the class's public contract.

front: Why is a stateless service object naturally thread-safe?
back: It has no mutable state shared between requests, so concurrent calls do not interfere through object fields.
accepted_answers: It has no mutable state shared between requests, so concurrent calls do not interfere through object fields.
hint: Local variables belong to each invocation.

front: Name the two classic forms of compound action that create race conditions.
back: Check-then-act and read-modify-write.
accepted_answers: ["check-then-act and read-modify-write","check then act and read modify write"]
hint: Lazy initialization is one example; incrementing a counter is another.

front: Why is `if (instance == null) instance = new Service();` unsafe when multiple threads execute it without synchronization?
back: The check and creation are separate operations, so multiple threads can observe null and construct different instances; publication may also be unsafe.
accepted_answers: The check and creation are separate operations, so multiple threads can observe null and construct different instances; publication may also be unsafe.
hint: This is a check-then-act sequence.

front: Why does making two individually thread-safe variables atomic not automatically preserve an invariant involving both variables?
back: An invariant spanning multiple variables requires the related reads and writes to occur as one atomic operation under a common synchronization policy.
accepted_answers: An invariant spanning multiple variables requires the related reads and writes to occur as one atomic operation under a common synchronization policy.
hint: Thread safety does not compose automatically across a compound action.

front: What two guarantees does locking provide for shared mutable state?
back: Mutual exclusion and memory visibility.
accepted_answers: ["mutual exclusion and visibility","atomicity and visibility"]
hint: Locks do more than prevent simultaneous execution.

front: A method synchronizes its entire body, including a slow network call that does not touch guarded state. What is wrong with this design?
back: It may be correct but holds the lock far longer than necessary, serializing unrelated requests and harming responsiveness and throughput.
accepted_answers: It may be correct but holds the lock far longer than necessary, serializing unrelated requests and harming responsiveness and throughput.
hint: Keep the critical section focused on shared state.

front: What does lock reentrancy mean?
back: A thread can acquire a lock it already holds, with an internal hold count, without deadlocking itself.
accepted_answers: ["the owning thread can acquire the same lock again","a thread may reacquire a lock it already holds","reentrant lock acquisition"]
hint: This allows synchronized methods to call other synchronized methods on the same object.

front: Why must every variable participating in one invariant be guarded by the same lock?
back: Otherwise another thread can observe or modify only part of the state transition, breaking the invariant even if each variable is sometimes locked.
accepted_answers: Otherwise another thread can observe or modify only part of the state transition, breaking the invariant even if each variable is sometimes locked.
hint: The lock protects a relationship, not just individual fields.

front: A counter uses `volatile int count` and increments with `count++`. Is it thread-safe?
back: No. Volatile provides visibility for reads and writes, but `count++` is a read-modify-write sequence and is not atomic.
accepted_answers: No. Volatile provides visibility for reads and writes, but `count++` is a read-modify-write sequence and is not atomic.
hint: Expand the increment into read, add, and write.

front: What is printed? `AtomicInteger n = new AtomicInteger(4); System.out.print(n.getAndIncrement() + ":" + n.get());`
hint: getAndIncrement returns the old value and then increments.

front: What is a stale read?
back: A thread reads an older value because no happens-before relationship guarantees visibility of a newer write.
accepted_answers: A thread reads an older value because no happens-before relationship guarantees visibility of a newer write.
hint: The write may have happened in real time but still be invisible.

front: When is `volatile` a good fit for shared state?
back: When updates do not depend on the current value, the variable is not part of a multi-variable invariant, and no other locking is required; status and lifecycle flags are common examples.
accepted_answers: When updates do not depend on the current value, the variable is not part of a multi-variable invariant, and no other locking is required; status and lifecycle flags are common examples.
hint: Visibility without compound atomicity.

front: What is wrong with registering an event listener from a constructor when the listener captures `this`?
back: The object can escape before construction finishes, allowing another thread to observe partially initialized state and invalidating initialization-safety guarantees.
accepted_answers: The object can escape before construction finishes, allowing another thread to observe partially initialized state and invalidating initialization-safety guarantees.
hint: Publication before the constructor returns is the core problem.

front: What is thread confinement?
back: Restricting an object so it is accessed by only one thread, eliminating the need for synchronization around that object.
accepted_answers: ["an object is accessed by only one thread","restricting state to a single thread","thread confinement"]
hint: The simplest shared-state bug is often avoided by not sharing.

front: Why is a JDBC `Connection` commonly safe to use during a request even when the connection object itself is not thread-safe?
back: The pool lends it to one request thread at a time, confining the connection until it is returned.
accepted_answers: The pool lends it to one request thread at a time, confining the connection until it is returned.
hint: The pool is shared; the checked-out connection is temporarily confined.

front: What conditions make an object immutable for concurrency purposes?
back: Its state cannot change after construction, all fields are final, and `this` does not escape during construction.
accepted_answers: Its state cannot change after construction, all fields are final, and `this` does not escape during construction.
hint: Unmodifiable state is not enough if construction is unsafe.

front: Why is a final reference to a mutable collection not enough to make the owning object immutable?
back: Final prevents reassignment of the reference, but the referenced collection can still be mutated unless it is defensively copied and never exposed for modification.
accepted_answers: Final prevents reassignment of the reference, but the referenced collection can still be mutated unless it is defensively copied and never exposed for modification.
hint: Final freezes the reference, not the object graph.

front: List four common safe-publication mechanisms.
back: Static initialization; storing into a volatile field or AtomicReference; storing into a final field of a properly constructed object; or accessing through a field guarded by a lock.
accepted_answers: Static initialization; storing into a volatile field or AtomicReference; storing into a final field of a properly constructed object; or accessing through a field guarded by a lock.
hint: Think class initialization, volatile/atomic, final construction, and locking.

front: What extra rule applies after safely publishing a mutable object?
back: Every later access must still follow its thread-safety policy: use the object's internal synchronization or hold the lock that guards it.
accepted_answers: Every later access must still follow its thread-safety policy: use the object's internal synchronization or hold the lock that guards it.
hint: Safe publication guarantees the initial visible state, not all future mutations.

front: Compare shared read-only, shared thread-safe, guarded, and thread-confined objects.
back: Shared read-only objects are never mutated; shared thread-safe objects synchronize internally; guarded objects require callers to hold a specified lock; thread-confined objects belong to one thread.
accepted_answers: Shared read-only objects are never mutated; shared thread-safe objects synchronize internally; guarded objects require callers to hold a specified lock; thread-confined objects belong to one thread.
hint: These are different rules of engagement for shared references.

front: What is printed? `Thread.currentThread().interrupt(); System.out.print(Thread.interrupted() + ":" + Thread.currentThread().isInterrupted());`
back: true:false
accepted_answers: true:false
hint: The static interrupted method reads and clears the current thread's status.

front: What three questions should you answer when designing a thread-safe class?
back: Identify the state variables, identify the invariants and postconditions involving them, and establish a synchronization policy for every access.
accepted_answers: Identify the state variables, identify the invariants and postconditions involving them, and establish a synchronization policy for every access.
hint: State, rules, and protection.

front: What is instance confinement?
back: Encapsulating mutable state inside an object and preventing its references from escaping, so the enclosing object's lock can guard it.
accepted_answers: ["encapsulating mutable state so it does not escape","mutable state confined within an owning object","instance confinement"]
hint: Private is useful only when references are not leaked.

front: When can a class delegate its thread safety to a concurrent collection?
back: When the collection independently protects all relevant state and no compound invariant spans it and other state that requires additional locking.
accepted_answers: When the collection independently protects all relevant state and no compound invariant spans it and other state that requires additional locking.
hint: Delegation works best when state variables are independent.

front: Why can returning a live mutable view of internal state break an otherwise thread-safe class?
back: Callers can mutate or iterate the state outside the class's synchronization policy, bypassing invariants and confinement.
accepted_answers: Callers can mutate or iterate the state outside the class's synchronization policy, bypassing invariants and confinement.
hint: Encapsulation includes controlling aliases.

front: You need to add a compound operation to a thread-safe class you do not own. Rank the safer extension strategies.
back: Prefer composition that adds its own synchronization; subclassing can work only when the locking policy is documented and stable; client-side locking is fragile because it depends on using the exact internal lock.
accepted_answers: Prefer composition that adds its own synchronization; subclassing can work only when the locking policy is documented and stable; client-side locking is fragile because it depends on using the exact internal lock.
hint: Do not guess another class's lock.

front: What concurrency information should a class document?
back: Its thread-safety guarantee, which lock guards each mutable variable, invariants, and any callbacks or methods that must not run while locks are held.
accepted_answers: Its thread-safety guarantee, which lock guards each mutable variable, invariants, and any callbacks or methods that must not run while locks are held.
hint: A synchronization policy is part of the maintainability contract.

front: Why is iterating a synchronized collection without holding its lock unsafe?
back: Each collection method is synchronized, but iteration is a compound action spanning many calls; concurrent modification can invalidate the traversal.
accepted_answers: Each collection method is synchronized, but iteration is a compound action spanning many calls; concurrent modification can invalidate the traversal.
hint: Method-level safety does not make a multi-step client action atomic.

front: What does a weakly consistent iterator guarantee?
back: It tolerates concurrent modification, reflects some stable traversal state, and may or may not include modifications made after iteration began.
accepted_answers: It tolerates concurrent modification, reflects some stable traversal state, and may or may not include modifications made after iteration began.
hint: It is neither a snapshot nor fail-fast.

front: When is `CopyOnWriteArrayList` a strong choice?
back: When traversal is far more frequent than modification, such as listener lists, because readers use immutable snapshots while each write copies the backing array.
accepted_answers: When traversal is far more frequent than modification, such as listener lists, because readers use immutable snapshots while each write copies the backing array.
hint: Excellent reads, expensive writes.

front: What design benefit does a `BlockingQueue` give a producer-consumer system?
back: It separates producers from consumers, provides thread-safe handoff, and can apply backpressure by blocking producers when bounded capacity is full.
accepted_answers: It separates producers from consumers, provides thread-safe handoff, and can apply backpressure by blocking producers when bounded capacity is full.
hint: The queue manages both coordination and capacity.

front: What is the difference between a latch and a barrier?
back: A latch waits for events and is normally one-shot; a barrier makes a group of threads rendezvous and can be reused for repeated phases.
accepted_answers: ["latch waits for events and is one-shot; barrier waits for threads and is reusable","latches wait for events; barriers wait for other threads"]
hint: CountDownLatch versus CyclicBarrier.

front: How can a semaphore bound a collection or service?
back: Acquire a permit before admitting an item or operation and release it when the item is removed or the operation finishes; the permit count represents remaining capacity.
accepted_answers: Acquire a permit before admitting an item or operation and release it when the item is removed or the operation finishes; the permit count represents remaining capacity.
hint: Capacity becomes a synchronization resource.

front: Why can a naive synchronized cache still compute the same expensive value twice?
back: If the expensive computation runs outside the lock, two misses can race and both compute; if it runs inside the lock, unrelated lookups serialize. A Future-based placeholder lets one computation represent the in-progress result.
accepted_answers: If the expensive computation runs outside the lock, two misses can race and both compute; if it runs inside the lock, unrelated lookups serialize. A Future-based placeholder lets one computation represent the in-progress result.
hint: Cache misses need coordination without holding a global lock during work.

front: Which concurrent-map operation should replace a client-side `containsKey` followed by `put`?
back: `putIfAbsent`.
accepted_answers: ["putIfAbsent","ConcurrentMap.putIfAbsent"]
hint: Use one atomic compound operation.
